definition: The arrival or approach of something momentous; specifically, in the Christian calendar, the four-week season of anticipatory waiting before Christmas, beginning on the Sunday nearest to the feast of Saint Andrew (November 30).
etymology: From Latin adventus, meaning a coming or arrival, itself from advenire: ad, meaning to, plus venire, meaning to come. Roman soldiers used adventus to describe the ceremonial arrival of an emperor into a city — the word carries that sense of a great presence drawing near, still not quite here, the whole world leaning forward.
usage: Today the first candle on the wreath is lit in millions of households, and the word Advent earns its keep not merely as a church-calendar label but as a precise name for that peculiar emotional weather — anticipation sharpened by darkness and cold — that no other English word quite captures.
